title: Universality of colimits of spaces
statement:
Use spaces, coherent diagrams, homotopy pullbacks and colimits from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix nested universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ and write $\mathcal S$ for the infinity category of $\mathcal U$-small spaces. Let $J$ be a $\mathcal U$-small simplicial indexing set, $B$ a small space, $F:J\to\mathcal S_{/B}$ a coherent diagram of spaces over $B$, and $f:A\to B$ a map of small spaces. Pullback preserves its colimit: the canonical map
$$\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}(A\times_B F(j))\longrightarrow A\times_B\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}F(j)$$
is an equivalence. The colimit on the right is formed over $B$, and the comparison is a map over $A$. Equivalently, $f^*:\mathcal S_{/B}\to\mathcal S_{/A}$ preserves all $\mathcal U$-small colimits, including the empty colimit.

source.place: Kerodon Tag 05V5, Corollary 7.7.3.23, universality of colimits in spaces (with the base-change meaning of universality); read online. No Stacks tag covers space-valued infinity categories.

proof.text: Let $U_B:\mathcal S_{/B}\to\mathcal S$ forget the structure arrow. The small-colimit theorem for spaces supplies the colimit of $U_BF$ for the given $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set $J$. The slice-colimit theorem, applied with $\mathcal C=\mathcal S$ and $x=B$, says that $U_B$ creates this colimit. Thus the given arrows and their coherent compatibilities induce $l:L\to B$ and a colimiting cocone $F\to\Delta_J(L,l)$ in $\mathcal S_{/B}$. Apply the same two results with $x=A$ to obtain all the small colimits in $\mathcal S_{/A}$, in particular a colimit $Q$ of $f^*F$. The hypotheses are only smallness of $J,A,B$; no nonempty or filtered indexing assumption is used.

source.place: Corollary 4.2.4.8 (small colimits of spaces) and Proposition 1.2.13.8 (colimits in overcategories); used to spell out the existing-colimit hypothesis in Kerodon 05V3. Online references through the two cited nodes; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text:
We record the slice mapping formulas needed for the construction. For $t:T\to B$ and $z:Z\to B$, apply the cone-category mapping formula with shape a point and diagram $B$. It gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{/B}(t,z)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{t}\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(T,Z)\xrightarrow{z\circ-}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(T,B)\bigr).$$
The object $1_B=(B,\mathrm{id}_B)$ is terminal since this fiber for $z=\mathrm{id}_B$ is contractible. Spaces have small limits by the cited limit theorem. If $X\to Z\leftarrow Y$ is a coherent cospan over $B$, form its homotopy pullback $P$ in spaces with the induced arrow $P\to B$. For any $T\to B$, the representable limit formula followed by the displayed fiber formula identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{/B}(T,P)$ with
$$\operatorname{Map}_{/B}(T,X)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_{/B}(T,Z)}\operatorname{Map}_{/B}(T,Y).$$
Indeed both sides specify maps to $X,Y$, their homotopy over $Z$, and the same specified homotopy to $t$ over $B$, including all higher compatibilities; taking these fibers and the pullback in either order imposes precisely the same data. The representable limit criterion therefore proves that $P$ is a pullback in the slice. These formulas are natural in all the displayed objects.

source.place: Proposition 7.7.3.19, finite limits in slices, with Example 7.6.2.43 cited there; the mapping-space calculation expands the slice universal property. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text:
For an arbitrary $p:Y\to A$, regard $a=(A,f)$ and $y=(Y,fp)$ as objects of $\mathcal C=\mathcal S_{/B}$. The slice-exponential theorem gives $E_y=[a,y]_B$, $E_a=[a,a]_B$, and the map $p^a:E_y\to E_a$ induced by $p$. Let $e:1_B\to E_a$ be the transpose of $\mathrm{id}_a:1_B\times_B a\to a$. Form in $\mathcal C$ the pullback
$$P_Y=1_B\times^h_{E_a}E_y,$$
using step 2. It is a small space over $B$. For any $T\to B$, the pullback mapping formula and the coherent exponential equivalences give
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Map}_{/B}(T,P_Y)
&\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{e\circ!}\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_{/B}(T,E_y)\to\operatorname{Map}_{/B}(T,E_a)\bigr)\\
&\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{\operatorname{pr}_A}\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_{/B}(T\times_B A,Y)\xrightarrow{p\circ-}\operatorname{Map}_{/B}(T\times_B A,A)\bigr)\\
&\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{/A}(T\times_B A,Y).
\end{aligned}$$
In the last line, a point is exactly a map to $Y$ over $B$ together with the homotopy $p h\simeq\operatorname{pr}_A$ in the slice over $B$; forgetting its redundant composite to $B$ is the same data as a map over $A$. Conversely, from a map over $A$ use the composite of its specified homotopy with $f$ as its homotopy over $B$, with the identity higher compatibility. After forgetting back to the map over $A$ this returns the original data. In the other composite the originally supplied compatibility over $B$ identifies the old homotopy with this composite one; the space of the redundant homotopy together with that identification is contractible. The same contraction with simplex parameters retains all higher compatibilities. Thus the cone mapping formula of step 2, applied to $\mathcal C$ and then to spaces, identifies the full spaces, rather than only their components. Currying sends $e\circ!$ to $\operatorname{pr}_A$, so the displayed equivalences respect precomposition in $T$ and postcomposition in $Y$. This constructs the objectwise dependent-product representation explicitly; no colimit-preservation assertion is assumed in its construction.

source.place: Proposition 7.7.3.19, expanded internal-Hom construction of the pullback right adjoint; the space-specific input is Proposition 7.7.3.17 (05UY). Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text:
For every test object $Y\to A$, apply step 3 to the cocone of step 1. The mapping-space criterion for colimits gives natural equivalences
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Map}_{/A}(f^*L,Y)
&\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{/B}(L,P_Y)\\
&\simeq\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{/B}(F(j),P_Y)\\
&\simeq\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{/A}(f^*F(j),Y).
\end{aligned}$$
Here the middle equivalence uses that $L$ is the slice colimit, not an assertion that pullback preserves it. Naturality of the currying and pullback equivalences in step 3 identifies the composite with restriction along the actual pulled-back cocone $f^*F\to\Delta_J f^*L$. The converse mapping-space criterion now says that this cocone is colimiting in $\mathcal S_{/A}$. This proves colimit preservation directly, rather than invoking an uncited theorem about infinity-categorical adjoints.

source.place: Corollary 7.7.3.20, preservation by the pullback left adjoint; this mapping-space proof spells out its appeal to Corollary 7.1.4.28. Combined with 05V3 and 05V5. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: The cocone with apex $Q$ of step 1 and the pulled-back cocone with apex $f^*L=A\times_B L$ are both initial objects of the same coherent cocone category. Its full subcategory of initial objects is a contractible Kan complex. Therefore the map induced by the second cocone from the first colimit is an equivalence. This is precisely the canonical comparison in the statement, since its composites with the colimit legs are the pulled-back legs by construction. It is a map over $A$, and the colimit defining $L$ remains the colimit in the slice over $B$.

source.place: Corollary 7.7.3.23, identification of universal colimits with the canonical base-change comparison. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: For $J=\varnothing$, the limits in step 4 are limits of empty diagrams of spaces and hence terminal spaces. Thus $f^*L$ is initial over $A$, just as $Q$ is, and the same comparison is an equivalence. In concrete terms the initial object in a space slice is $\varnothing\to B$ and $A\times_B\varnothing=\varnothing$. Consequently the proof includes the empty colimit; it also needs neither a point of $A$ nor a point of $B$.

source.place: Corollary 7.7.3.23; empty-shape case of the mapping-space argument above. Read online; not archived in literature/.
